newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, October 15 - Haifa - Five vessels due, 1-2 days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth, up to 4 general cargo, up to 1 bulk cargo, 4 containers, 2 tankers, 3 passenger vessels. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 1 general cargo, 1 bulk, 1 container, 2 bunkering and 2 tankers, 4 vessels under repair/drydock, 4 awaiting orders. Ashdod - One to two days delay for vessels due. Loading/discharging at berth, up to 5 general cargo, 3 bulk, 3 containers, passenger vessel. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 1 general cargo, 2 bulk. Eilat - One bulker loading/discharging at berth, 2 passenger vessels, 1 bulk waiting at anchorage to load/discharge.
JORDAN, October 12 - Aqaba - No vessels due, 3 loading at berth, 5 discharging at berth. 4 Vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 3 awaiting orders.

MOZAMBIQUE, October 14 - Nacala - Port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restriction of 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tugboat available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally (first come, first served basis). Container terminal/other terminals working normally. Pilotage is now possible. 24 Hours delay for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugboats now fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. Maputo - Pilotage is now possible 24 hours a day. Two tugboats available, one out of order. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so (first come, first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9 metres less 0.5 metre plus rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, October 14 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.

SIERRA LEONE, October 15 - Freetown - Vessels due, 1 heavy lift general cargo discharger, 3 container dischargers, no delays expected. Vessels discharging/loading at berth, vehicle and container discharger, 3 rice dischargers. Vessels anchored, 1 rice discharger, 1 other vessel.

SOUTH AFRICA, October 14 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths congested, with delays of approx. 24 hours at present. Bulk import berths congested, with delays of approx. 30 hours on berth 702. Bull export berths (minerals, etc.) congested with delays of approx. 72 hours at present. Bulk coal berths, 4 vessels alongside, 4 anchored, 12 due by 21/10. Berthing delays of 2-3 days at present. Durban - Container terminal - Delays of up to 36 hours at present. Point/New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo, but delays for wheat dischargers can be expected. Maize terminal (Maydon Wharf 8) - 1 Maize loader for October and 2 for November. Citrus, season closing end-October. Bunker supplies tight, delays in supplying of bunker can be expected due to bunching of vessels. Drydock and floating dock - Fully booked for October and 70 percent booked for November.

East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Extremely busy, but no delays expected. Drydock fully booked for October and November. Copper moving in containers to Far East. Elevator - 1 Vessel due mid-November. Gasoil pipeline - Under-utilised. Wheat imports - 3 Vessels due by 20/10. Tankers busy for next 2-3 months. Port Elizabeth - Three vessels in port. No delays expected for fruit, ore, general or tanker berths. Container berths - 8 Vessels due by 20/10, no delays expected. Cape Town - Breakbulk berths - No delays, vessels working on arrival. Container terminal - No delays expected for the coming week. Bunker berths - No delays expected. Drydock and repair quay fully occupied and booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Working normally.

TUNISIA, October 12 - Sousse - One vessel discharging general cargo, no waiting time. No vessels awaiting orders. Gabes - Three vessels loading at berth of which 1 bulk fertiliser, 2 acid tankers, 1 bagged phosphate awaiting orders. Sfax - Five vessels in port of which discharging, 1 bulk sulphur, 1 bulk maize, 1 fuel oil, 1 soyabean oil. 1 Vessel loading bulk tsp. Tunis - Two general cargo vessels in port, 1 vessel awaiting ship owner's instructions. Rades - Three ro/ro in port. Goulette - North side - 1 General cargo, 1 passenger vessel, 1 military vessel. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 motor tanker. 1 Vessel in roads. October 15 - Bizerta - Three vessels operating of which 1 discharging fuel oil, 2 steel. No delays. Zarzis - No vessels, no delays.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, October 13 - Dubai - Vessels operating in port from 6/10 to 12/10, 80 container vessels, 10 general cargo, 4 general cargo/container vessels, 6 bulk carriers, 7 car carriers, 16 tankers, 5 naval vessels, 3 UAE naval vessels, 5 bunkers/repairs/stores, etc., 8 dhows, 13 barges, 12 tugs, 24 supply boats, 2 lpg tankers.

YEMEN, October 13 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied, 7 vessels alongside of which 1 bulk corn, 1 wheat flour, 1 steel, 1 general cargo/containers, 1 containers, 1 general cargo. 1 General cargo loading, 2 vessels anchored of which 1 bulk corn/soya, 1 bulk wheat. Berthing waiting time, general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargo up to 4 days, bulk cargo up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - Two vessels discharging of which 1 palm oil, 1 wheat flour. No vessels anchored, 1 days berthing waiting time.
